To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of prophylactic antibiotics during simultaneous growth of bacteria and osteoblast-like human cells on a poly(methyl) methacrylate (PMMA) surface results in survival of the cells.
the presence of cefotaxim in vitro resulted in survival of human osteoblasts during growth with highly virulent S.aureus, while the bacteria showed delayed growth.

the presence of cefazolin for 8 hours resulted in survival of osteoblasts in a model mimicking peri-operative contamination of an acrylic implant with Staphylococci, but that the bacteria did not die, but showed a delayed growth, which may explain the recalcitrant nature of biofilms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of prophilactic antibiotic treatment on the tissue integration versus bacterial colonization on a poly(methylmethacrylate) (PMMA) surface.
the development of an in vitro model that allows the study of BAI.
the influence of prophilactically given cefotaxim on tissue integration versus bacterial colonization on a poly(methylmethacrylate) (PMMA) surface in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prophylactic use of antibiotics may be beneficial for tissue integration, but may also lead to a delayed growth of adhering bacteria.
the prophylactic use of antibiotics in orthopedic surgery should be reconsidered.
the presence of cefazolin during the first 8 h after implantation is not sufficient to prevent bacterial colonization and subsequent BAI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prophylaxis with cephatholin did not prevent bacterial colonization, but it prevented bacterial overgrowth.
cephatholin is not able to eliminate S. aureus from an implant surface in the presence of U-2OS cells.
the use of prophylactic antibiotics can be beneficial to prevent BAI in the early stages of implant integration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of antibiotics in the peri-operative period may not be sufficient to prevent BAI, as it does not prevent the colonization of the implant by bacteria.
cephatholin did not prevent bacterial colonization but rather delayed it.
prophylactically administered cephatholin did not prevent S. aureus colonization of the PMMA surface, but it did prevent U-2 OS from dying and enabled the cells to grow on the surface.
